bio: I am an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at UNC Charlotte, leading the High-Performance Data Intensive (HPDi) Lab. My research focuses on high-performance computing and scientific data management, especially data reduction, compression, and parallel and distributed systems.

I earned my Ph.D. at NJIT with Qing Liu and my bachelor's degree at Shandong University. I interned at Los Alamos National Laboratory (2022–2023) and am affiliated with Charlotte's High Performance Computing and Systems Lab.

projects.deepcq: A two-stage deep-surrogate framework for predicting lossy compression quality. Reusable features support configuration selection across compressors, metrics, and scientific datasets without a full compression sweep.
projects.qualitynet: Fast surrogate models estimate compression quality to guide configuration choices for scientific datasets.
projects.genesis: Phase I research in the first DOE Genesis Mission cohort, connecting artificial intelligence and scientific computing.
